capabilities.handling: Use an immutable reviewed image; the authored reference uses the existing base-image pin.
limitations: The reference is not a released Realm profile image.
Image validity does not prove installed capability content.

capabilities.handling: Realm image construction can feed a Dev Container projection; paths are relative to the configuration directory.
limitations: The #10 generator owns emission.
Build arguments must not embed credentials.

capabilities.handling: Consumer application orchestration owns Compose files and service selection.
limitations: Do not infer Compose services from the privileged services profile.
Host and service orchestration require separate execution proof.

capabilities.handling: Prefer reviewed reusable Features when an immutable artifact and its option contract are available.
limitations: Require digest-bound OCI references in this reference policy.
The official base schema does not validate arbitrary Feature options.

capabilities.handling: Keep container-wide environment separate from tool-spawned process environment and host-supplied values.
limitations: Never put credential values in generated files or reports.
localEnv refers to the selected host, including a cloud host.

capabilities.handling: Preserve non-root image identity and distinguish container process users from remote tool users.
limitations: UID/GID adjustment is Linux-specific.
The reference disables UID mutation; identity existence needs runtime proof.
The privileged safety flag does not encode a user or UID/GID policy.

capabilities.handling: Repository workspace requirements are consumer intent; host adapters own filesystem-specific bindings.
limitations: Codespaces ignores ordinary bind mounts.
Do not expose host sockets or privileged paths through an implicit profile default.

capabilities.handling: Lifecycle commands are reviewed consumer code; validation never executes them.
limitations: initializeCommand runs on the host and may repeat.
Strings use a shell, arrays direct execution, and objects parallel commands.

capabilities.handling: Forwarding is separate from application listening and host port publication.
limitations: Codespaces does not support host:port forwarding syntax.
UI forwarding and reachability need host-specific proof.

capabilities.handling: Declare minimum host needs without claiming the selected machine or GPU satisfies them.
limitations: Machine selection and GPU devices remain host responsibilities.
Requirements are not resource-allocation or accelerator proof.

capabilities.handling: Editor settings stay in a uniquely named customization namespace.
limitations: The reference CLI may ignore editor-specific settings.
Extensions and editor availability need separate reviewed qualification.

capabilities.handling: Codespaces-specific UI and repository permission intent stays in its host namespace.
limitations: Namespace presence grants no repository access.
A host adapter and explicit authorization own permissions and paid resources.

capabilities.handling: Relay owns CI/prebuild mechanics; cache identity must not become canonical capability truth.
limitations: Codespaces prebuild configuration is host/service-specific.
A cache hit or prebuild is not runtime conformance.
Documented reference implementation behavior is not complete Realm runtime qualification.
Editor customizations and host adapters are outside CLI conformance.
Interpreting ports and requirements does not provide a forwarding proxy or allocate a machine.
Clone-in-volume behavior changes workspace mount assumptions.
No VS Code session is established by offline validation.
Host means the cloud VM; bind mounts, shutdown and forwarding semantics differ.
No paid Codespaces creation, machine selection, connect or rebuild proof is claimed.
A supporting-tool listing does not prove field-level compatibility.
A reviewed implementation/version and provider-specific run are required.
